Use `snl migrate` only when `snl info` shows that the workspace needs an explicit schema migration.

### Availability
This Entry is a normative product contract. The command is implemented only when its canonical path appears in machine-readable `snl --help`; absence means planned and unavailable, never silently emulated through a different command.


### Command path
`migrate` is the canonical transport-neutral command. The intended shell spelling is `snl migrate`. Current availability is advertised by machine-readable `snl --help`; an Agent/MCP adapter submits the same operation object instead of reconstructing shell text.

### Operation request
```json
{"protocol":"snl.operation/v1","command":"migrate","root":"/absolute/workspace","arguments":{"targetVersion":"<version>","expectedWorkspaceRevision":"<opaque>","dryRun":false}}
```
Every adapter accepts exactly this semantic request. Unknown argument keys are rejected. The CLI accepts `--root` and `--json` globally and emits one complete JSON document followed by a newline. Unknown, future, malformed, lossy, or already-diverged sources fail closed.

### Success result
A successful call exits `0` and returns `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":true,"command":"migrate","data":{},"diagnostics":[]}`. `data` contains source/target versions, deterministic migration steps, receipt, and resulting revision.

### Failure and exit semantics
Domain rejection (invalid data, not-found, conflict, or validation errors) exits `1`. Invocation, input I/O, unsupported workspace/schema, lock acquisition, and runtime failures exit `2`. Failure stdout under `--json` is exactly one `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":false,"command":"migrate","error":{"code":"<stable-code>","message":"<actionable text>","details":{},"retryable":false}}`; no stack trace or prose contaminates stdout.

### State and concurrency
Mutating only when `dryRun` is false. Bind the reviewed source revision under the writer lock and publish config/version last. Revisions, cursors, checked digests, and workspace revisions are opaque tokens. After success, canonical readback and whole-workspace validation must observe the published state.
